nodes.label: Go/No-Go Gate
nodes.rationale: Step 4 of the build plan is explicitly framed as 'the actual go/no-go gate' — running real build/trading questions manually decides whether the RAG pipeline is good enough to proceed, rather than relying on automated metrics alone.

nodes.label: Headhunter (unique item, trade pricing)
nodes.rationale: Live trade pricing is explicitly excluded from v1 scope per the build plan — deferred as a stretch goal because 'prices too volatile to embed', so the system should decline/flag rather than fabricate a price.

nodes.label: Per-Entry Chunking (Step 3 assumption)
nodes.rationale: Chunking each corpus entry (item/gem/mod) individually was the Step 3 design assumption; Questions 4-7 (cross-referencing) exist specifically to test whether this granularity is sufficient for retrieval or whether chunking needs revisiting.

nodes.label: Hallucination Check (numeric precision)
nodes.rationale: Questions 8-9 test exact numeric recall (item level, armour value) because wrong numbers are considered worse than no answer for a build advisor.

nodes.label: Honesty Behavior (out-of-scope handling)
nodes.rationale: Questions 10-12 are a pass/fail check on honesty: the system confidently fabricating answers for out-of-scope questions is treated as a red flag regardless of how well the direct/cross-referencing/precision questions perform.
